Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-4589", "title": "Eosinophilic Disorders", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Eosinophils are a type of white blood cell."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "They help fight off infections and play a role in your body's immune response."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "They can also build up and cause inflammation."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Normally your blood doesn't have a large number of eosinophils."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Your body may produce more of them in response to: Allergic disorders Skin conditions Parasitic and fungal infections Autoimmune diseases Some cancers Bone marrow disorders In some conditions, the eosinophils can move outside the bloodstream and build up in organs and tissues."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "This can happen in many different parts of the body, including the esophagus , heart, lungs, blood, and intestines."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Treatment of eosinophilic disorders can vary, depending on the cause and which part of the body is affected."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Steroids are often part of the treatment."}]}, {"id": "MLP-3229", "title": "Mpox", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Mpox, which used to be called monkeypox, is a disease caused by the monkeypox virus."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "This virus is in the same family of viruses as the smallpox virus."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Mpox can be spread between animals and people, but it's mainly spread through close contact with someone who has it."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It is found regularly in parts of Central, Eastern and West Africa."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "The virus that causes it has been found in small rodents, monkeys, and other mammals that live in these areas."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Some outbreaks of mpox have affected people in many countries around the world, including the United States."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "What are the types of monkeypox viruses?"}, {"id": "S007", "text": "There are two types of monkeypox viruses: Clade I is regularly found in Central and Eastern Africa."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "It causes more severe illness and deaths than clade II."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Clade II is regularly found in West Africa."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Infections from clade II are less severe."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Most people who get this type will survive."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "This type is the cause of the global mpox outbreak that peaked in 2022 but has continued to decrease."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Mpox spreads in different ways: Through close, personal contact with someone who has the virus: Through direct contact with their rash, scabs, or body fluids By breathing in the virus during prolonged, face-to-face contact During intimate physical contact such as kissing, cuddling, hugging, massage or sex During pregnancy, from the mother to the fetus."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "From touching items (such as clothes, bedding, or towels) that were used by someone who has the virus From infected animals: By being scratched or bitten by the animal By preparing or eating meat or using products from the animal Someone who has mpox can spread it from the time their symptoms start until their rash has fully healed, all scabs have fallen off, and a fresh layer of skin has formed."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Researchers have found that some people can spread mpox to others from 1 to 4 days before their symptoms appear."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "The symptoms of mpox usually start within 3 weeks from the time you were exposed to the virus."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "The symptoms may include: A rash with sores that can look like pimples or blisters."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "It could be on the face, inside the mouth, and on other parts of the body, like the hands, feet, chest, genitals, or anus."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "It goes through different stages, including scabs, before healing."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Respiratory symptoms, such as a sore throat, nasal congestion, or cough ."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "You may have all or only a few symptoms: You may get a rash first, followed by other symptoms You may have flu-like symptoms and then develop a rash 1-4 days later You may only get a rash How is mpox diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S022", "text": "To find out if you have mpox, your health care provider: Will ask about your symptoms and medical history."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Will take a sample of tissue from one of the sores so it can be tested for the monkeypox virus."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "May do blood tests to check for monkeypox virus or for antibodies to the virus."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Antibodies are proteins that your immune system makes to fight foreign substances such as viruses and bacteria ."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "There are no treatments specifically for mpox, but many people get better on their own."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Since mpox and smallpox are similar, antiviral medicines that treat smallpox may also help treat mpox."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Antiviral medicines may be recommended for people have severe mpox or are at risk of severe mpox, for example because they: Have immune system , for example from HIV or other conditions Are pregnant Are children, especially those under age 1 Have certain active skin conditions that can cause widespread infection, such as eczema , impetigo , or psoriasis If you have mpox, it is recommended that you stay home from the time you have symptoms until your mpox rash has healed and a new layer of skin has formed."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "It would be best to stay in a separate room from your family members and pets if you can."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "JYNNEOS is a vaccine that can help prevent mpox (and smallpox)."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "The vaccine is given in two doses 4 weeks apart."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Getting both doses gives the best protection."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "The vaccine is recommended for people who are at risk of mpox, for example because they: Had or think they could've had exposure to someone with mpox Are a man who has sex with men, who in the last 6 months had: One or more sexually transmitted infections (STIs) More than one sexual partner Sex at a commercial sex venue (like a sex club or bathhouse) Sex at a large public event where people had spread mpox Had a sex partner who is at risk of mpox Expect to be in any of these situations Are at risk of exposure at work, for example at a lab or healthcare facility Will be traveling to an area where there is an outbreak and, while there, will likely have sex: With a new partner At a commercial sex venue or large public event In exchange for money or drugs Check with your provider to see if the vaccine is recommended for you."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "There are also other steps you can take to help prevent mpox: Avoid close, skin-to-skin contact with the mpox rash."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "So, while a person is sick with mpox: Do not touch their rash or scabs Do not kiss, hug, cuddle, or have sex with them Avoid contact with items that were used by someone who has mpox: Do not touch the bedding, towels, or clothing of a person who has mpox Do not share eating utensils or cups with them If you or someone you live with has mpox, clean and disinfect your home Wash your hands often with soap and water or use an alcohol-based hand sanitizer, especially after contact with sick people."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-191", "title": "Cleft Lip and Palate", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Cleft lip and cleft palate are birth defects that occur when a baby's lip or mouth do not form properly."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "A baby can have a cleft lip, a cleft palate, or both."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "A cleft lip happens if the tissue that makes up the lip does not join completely before birth."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "This causes an opening in the upper lip."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "The opening can be a small slit or a large opening that goes through the lip into the nose."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "It can be on one or both sides of the lip or, rarely, in the middle of the lip."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Children with a cleft lip also can have a cleft palate."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "The roof of the mouth is called the \"palate.\" With a cleft palate, the tissue that makes up the roof of the mouth does not join correctly."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Babies may have both the front and back parts of the palate open, or they may have only one part open."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Children with a cleft lip or a cleft palate often have problems with feeding and talking."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "They also might have ear infections, hearing loss, and problems with their teeth."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Often, surgery can close the lip and palate."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Cleft lip surgery is usually done before age 12 months, and cleft palate surgery is done before 18 months."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "They may need additional surgeries, dental and orthodontic care, and speech therapy as they get older."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "With treatment, most children with clefts do well and lead a healthy life."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention"}]}, {"id": "MLP-6051", "title": "Dehydration", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Dehydration is a condition caused by the loss of too much fluid from the body ."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It happens when you are losing more fluids than you are taking in, and your body does not have enough fluids to work properly."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "You can become dehydrated because of: Diarrhea Vomiting Sweating too much Urinating too much, which can happen because of certain medicines and illnesses Fever Not drinking enough water or other fluids Who is more likely to develop dehydration?"}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Certain people are more likely to develop dehydration: Older adults."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Some people lose their sense of thirst as they age, so they don't drink enough fluids."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Infants and young children, who are more likely to have diarrhea or vomiting People with chronic illnesses that cause them to urinate or sweat more often, such as diabetes , cystic fibrosis , or kidney problems People who take medicines that cause them to urinate or sweat more People who exercise or work outdoors during hot weather What are the symptoms of dehydration?"}, {"id": "S006", "text": "In adults , the symptoms of dehydration include: Feeling very thirsty Dry mouth Urinating and sweating less than usual Dark-colored urine Dry skin Feeling tired Dizziness In infants and young children , the symptoms of dehydration include: Dry mouth and tongue Crying without tears No wet diapers for 3 hours or more A high fever Being unusually sleepy or drowsy Irritability Eyes that look sunken Dehydration can be mild, or it can be severe enough to be life-threatening."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Get medical help right away if the symptoms also include: Confusion Fainting Lack of urination Rapid heartbeat Rapid breathing Shock How is dehydration diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S008", "text": "To find out if you dehydration, your health care provider will: Do a physical exam Check your vital signs Ask about your symptoms Your provider may also order tests, such as: Blood tests to check your electrolyte levels, especially potassium and sodium ."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Electrolytes are minerals in your body that have an electric charge."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "They have many important jobs, including helping to keep a balance of fluids in your body."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Blood tests to check your kidney function ."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Urine tests to check for dehydration and its cause."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "What are the treatments for dehydration?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The treatment for dehydration is to replace the fluids and electrolytes that you have lost."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "For mild cases, you may just need to drink lots of water."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "If you lost electrolytes, sports drinks may help."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "There are also oral rehydration solutions for children."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "You can buy those without a prescription."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Severe cases may be treated with intravenous (IV) fluids with salt in a hospital."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "The key to preventing dehydration is making sure that you get enough fluids: Drink enough water every day."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Each person's needs can be different, so ask your health care provider how much you should be drinking each day."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Avoid drinks that have sugar and caffeine ."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Drink extra fluids when the weather is hot, especially if you are exercising or working outside."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "If you are losing a lot of minerals in sweat, sports drinks can help you."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "But some sports drinks have lots of sugar, so be careful not to drink too much of them."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "If you are having trouble keeping liquids down, you can try taking small sips of water or sucking on ice chips."}]}, {"id": "MLP-490", "title": "Exercise and Physical Fitness", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "What are the basics of exercise and physical fitness?"}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Exercise is anything that gets your body moving."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Regular exercise is one of the best things you can do for your health."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "It has many benefits , including improving your overall health and fitness, and reducing your risk for many chronic (long-term) diseases."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Every physical fitness routine is built on a few simple ideas."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "These include: Make exercise a habit, as your body adapts to the type of activity you do most often."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Build up your activity level slowly to help you continue to get stronger, faster, or more flexible without pushing too hard all at once."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Challenge yourself by lifting slightly heavier weights, adding a few more minutes to your walk, or increasing your pace."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Mix up your workouts to keep things interesting and help prevent injuries or burnout."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Show up regularly, even for short sessions, to help you continue to make progress."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "What are the different types of exercise?"}, {"id": "S011", "text": "There are many different types of exercise."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Before you start, check with your health care provider, especially if you have trouble moving, balancing, or worry that exercise might not be safe for you."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "A few main types of exercise include: Aerobic exercises such as walking, running, or swimming are sometimes referred to as cardio."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "This is short for cardiovascular exercise."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "These exercises increase your breathing and heart rate."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "They keep your heart, lungs, and circulatory system healthy and improve your overall fitness."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Strength, or resistance training, exercises use weights, resistance bands, or your own body weight to build stronger muscles."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Balance exercises, such as tai chi or standing on one leg, improve your stability and coordination."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "They may make it easier for you to walk on uneven surfaces and help prevent falls ."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Flexibility exercises, such as stretching or yoga, help your joints move more easily and improve your posture."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Most people benefit from a combination of these types of exercises."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Your provider can help you choose the best type or amount of activity for you based on your fitness level and health."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "Fitting regular exercise into your daily schedule may seem difficult at first."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "But you can start slowly and break your exercise time into chunks."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Even small amounts of exercise can be helpful."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "You can work your way up to doing the recommended amount of exercise."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "How much exercise you need depends on your age and health."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "To get started, you don't need fancy equipment, but having the right tools can make it easier and more fun."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "There are a variety of places where you can exercise and create a routine that fits your lifestyle."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Dumbbells, kettlebells, a mat, or resistance bands are versatile and affordable options for strength training and stretching."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "A treadmill, a stationary bike, or a workout video are a few options for indoor cardio."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "These places offer equipment, classes, and sometimes personal trainers for guidance and support."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Ask if you can try the center before you join, and if staff are available to show you how to use the exercise equipment."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Try riding a bike, walking your dog, or exploring local parks and trails."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Dress for the weather and protect yourself from the sun ."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "If safety is a concern, choose a well-lit neighborhood, a busy park, or even an indoor shopping mall for your walk."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Include activities that strengthen all parts of your body, especially your core, which are the muscles in your abdomen (belly), back, and hips."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "A strong core helps with balance and stability and can lower your risk of back injuries ."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "If you haven't exercised in a while , start slowly and talk to your provider if you have health concerns."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "If you don't feel right, or have any pain, extreme shortness of breath , or dizziness , stop exercising and seek help right away."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Even with the best intentions, it's easy to fall off track."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "Here are some ways to keep going: Choose activities you enjoy."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "It's easier to make exercise a regular part of your life if you have fun doing it."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "Use the proper equipment to prevent injuries , listen to your body, and don't overdo it."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Your goals should be challenging, but realistic."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "It may be helpful to reward yourself when you reach them."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "The rewards could be something big, like new workout gear, or something smaller, such as a new water bottle or movie tickets."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Try a new class, playlist, Podcast, or outdoor route when things get stale."}, {"id": "S049", "text": "Exercise with a friend, join a group challenge, or check in with an online community."}, {"id": "S050", "text": "A pedometer or an app like a fitness tracker on your phone or other device can help you track your progress."}]}]
